description: Low-level crypto primitive contracts for std/crypto that verify structural safety properties without claiming cryptographic strength. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/crypto/primitives — verified crypto primitives'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/core.mm and std/crypto/*.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT model real hashes, signatures, randomness, or timing; expose bounded deterministic witnesses and validation predicates that downstream modules can compose.
implementation_notes: Every predicate result is an i64 boolean constrained to 0 or 1.
State clearly in comments that these are structural contracts, not cryptographic security proofs.
Use explicit byte/length bounds and avoid arrays or byte-string internals unless existing std/crypto modules already expose the same syntax.

atoms.name: is_valid_key_len
atoms.description: Return 1 when a key length is inside caller-approved inclusive bounds, otherwise 0.

atoms.name: is_valid_nonce_len
atoms.description: Validate a nonce length against a positive expected length.

atoms.name: constant_time_eq_flag
atoms.description: Return an i64 boolean equality witness for two bounded scalar digests. The contract is structural and does not model physical timing.

atoms.name: digest_len_ok
atoms.description: Validate that a digest length is positive and no larger than a protocol cap.
